text: On Sennet Point, where spray still whitens the black rocks below the cliffs, the old lighthouse stands as a sealed reminder of a busy maritime age. According to the Northfold Maritime Archive, the Sennet Lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987, ending 114 years of service to the peninsula and its treacherous eastern channel. Keepers had already been reduced to a single rotating crew by the early 1980s, after radar and automated beacons made the lantern less necessary. Built in 1873 from local stone and later fitted with a cast-iron lantern room, it guided coal steamers, trawlers and mail packets through fog that could roll in within minutes. Today, its lens has been removed, but the tower remains a quiet landmark.
